questions.q: Simplify: $48 \div 6 \times 4 + 14 - 20 \div 5$
questions.solution:
$\div$ and $\times$ first, left to right: $48 \div 6 \times 4 = 8 \times 4 = 32$, and $20 \div 5 = 4$.
So $32 + 14 - 4 = 42$.

**Answer: 42**
questions.shortcut: Do $\div$/$\times$ left to right before $+$/$-$: $32 + 14 - 4 = 42$.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $13^{45} \times 17^{99}$?
questions.solution:
Only unit digits matter: $3^{45}$ and $7^{99}$.
Cycle of 3 is 3, 9, 7, 1; $45 \div 4$ leaves remainder 1, so $3^{45}$ ends in 3.
Cycle of 7 is 7, 9, 3, 1; $99 \div 4$ leaves remainder 3, so $7^{99}$ ends in 3.
Unit digit $= 3 \times 3 = 9$.

**Answer: 9**
questions.shortcut: Work with unit digits only: the two cycles give $3 \times 3 = 9$.
questions.pattern: unit digit of a product of powers

questions.q: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 720. If one of the numbers is 144, what is the other number?
questions.solution:
HCF $\times$ LCM $=$ product of the numbers: $12 \times 720 = 144 \times N$.
$N = \frac{12 \times 720}{144} = 60$.

**Answer: 60**
questions.shortcut: Other number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ the given number.

questions.q: In an office, 60% of the employees are males. If 40% of the males and 30% of the females receive a travel allowance, what per cent of all the employees receive a travel allowance?
questions.solution:
Take 100 employees: 60 males and 40 females.
Allowance holders $= 40\%$ of $60 + 30\%$ of $40 = 24 + 12 = 36$.

**Answer: 36%**
questions.shortcut: $0.6 \times 0.4 + 0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.36$, i.e. 36% — the total is not needed.

questions.q: A sum of ₹6,800 is divided among A, B and C such that $A : B = 3 : 4$ and $B : C = 2 : 5$. What is C's share?
questions.solution:
Make B the same in both ratios: $A : B = 3 : 4$ and $B : C = 4 : 10$, so $A : B : C = 3 : 4 : 10$.
C's share $= \frac{10}{17} \times 6800 = ₹4{,}000$.

**Answer: ₹4,000**
questions.shortcut: Link the ratios through B, then take $\frac{10}{17}$ of the total.
questions.pattern: two linked ratios, share of one part

questions.q: The average age of 30 students of a class is 14 years. When the age of the teacher is included, the average increases by 1 year. What is the age of the teacher?
questions.solution:
Total age of the students $= 30 \times 14 = 420$ years.
With the teacher: $31 \times 15 = 465$ years.
Teacher's age $= 465 - 420 = 45$ years.

**Answer: 45 years**
questions.shortcut: Each of the 30 students gains 1 year plus the teacher's own 15: $30 + 15 = 45$.
questions.pattern: average rises when one member joins

questions.q: What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for $1\frac{1}{2}$ years at 10% per annum, interest compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
Rate per half-year $= 5\%$; number of half-years $= 3$.
Amount $= 8000\left(\frac{21}{20}\right)^3 = ₹9{,}261$.
CI $= 9261 - 8000 = ₹1{,}261$.

**Answer: ₹1,261**
questions.shortcut: Half-yearly means 3 slots at 5%: $8000 \times \frac{21}{20} \times \frac{21}{20} \times \frac{21}{20} = 9261$.

questions.q: A trader allows a discount of 25% on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20%. If the cost price of the article is ₹720, what is its marked price?
questions.pattern: find MP from profit and discount

questions.q: A dishonest shopkeeper sells goods at the cost price but uses a false weight of 800 g instead of 1 kg. What is his gain per cent?
questions.solution:
He charges for 1000 g but gives only 800 g, so he gains 200 g on every 800 g sold.
Gain% $= \frac{200}{800} \times 100 = 25\%$.

**Answer: 25%**
questions.shortcut: Gain% $= \frac{\text{error}}{\text{true weight} - \text{error}} \times 100 = \frac{200}{800} \times 100$.

questions.q: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days can A, B and C together complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Pair rates: $\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{5+4+3}{60} = \frac{1}{5}$, which counts every person twice.
So the rate of $(A+B+C) = \frac{1}{10}$ per day $\Rightarrow$ 10 days.

**Answer: 10 days**
questions.shortcut: Add the three pair rates and halve: $\frac{1}{5} \div 2 = \frac{1}{10}$.

questions.q: A pump can fill a tank in 2 hours. Because of a leak in the tank, it took $2\frac{1}{3}$ hours to fill it. In how much time can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.solution:
Filling rate with the leak $= \frac{3}{7}$ tank/hour; pump rate $= \frac{1}{2}$.
Leak rate $= \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{7} = \frac{1}{14}$ tank/hour.
The leak empties the full tank in 14 hours.

**Answer: 14 hours**
questions.shortcut: Leak time $= \frac{\text{pump time} \times \text{actual time}}{\text{difference}} = \frac{2 \times \frac{7}{3}}{\frac{1}{3}} = 14$ hours.

questions.q: A car covers the first half of the distance between two towns at 60 km/h and the second half at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
For equal distances, average speed $= \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \frac{2 \times 60 \times 40}{100} = 48$ km/h.
(The simple mean 50 km/h is the trap.)

**Answer: 48 km/h**
questions.shortcut: Equal halves $\Rightarrow$ harmonic mean: $\frac{2 \times 60 \times 40}{60 + 40} = 48$.

questions.q: A man can row at 10 km/h in still water. He rows 24 km upstream and 24 km downstream, taking 5 hours in all. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution:
$\frac{24}{10 - x} + \frac{24}{10 + x} = 5 \Rightarrow 24 \times \frac{20}{100 - x^2} = 5$.
$\frac{480}{100 - x^2} = 5 \Rightarrow 100 - x^2 = 96 \Rightarrow x^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 2$ km/h.

**Answer: 2 km/h**
questions.shortcut: Equal distances up and down: time $= \frac{2ds}{s^2 - x^2} = \frac{480}{100 - x^2} = 5$.

questions.q: In what ratio must rice costing ₹48 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹65 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹56 per kg?
questions.solution:
Alligation: (dearer $-$ mean) : (mean $-$ cheaper) $= (65 - 56) : (56 - 48) = 9 : 8$.
So the ratio of ₹48 rice to ₹65 rice is $9 : 8$.

**Answer: 9 : 8**
questions.shortcut: Cross-subtract the prices: the differences 9 and 8 are the weights of the cheaper and dearer rice.

questions.q: If $x + \frac{1}{x} = 4$, what is the value of $x^5 + \frac{1}{x^5}$?
O is the circumcentre of $\triangle ABC$. If $\angle OBC = 30^\circ$ and $\angle OCB = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle OBC$, $\angle BOC = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 20^\circ = 130^\circ$.
The central angle on chord $BC$ is twice the angle at the circumference: $\angle BAC = \frac{130^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ$.

**Answer: 65°**
questions.shortcut: Central angle = 180 − (the two given base angles), then halve it.

questions.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and drawn into a cylindrical wire of radius 1 mm. What is the length of the wire?
questions.solution:
Volume of the sphere $= \frac{4}{3}\pi (3)^3 = 36\pi$ cm³.
Wire radius $= 0.1$ cm, so $\pi (0.1)^2 \times L = 36\pi \Rightarrow L = \frac{36}{0.01} = 3600$ cm $= 36$ m.

**Answer: 36 m**
questions.shortcut: $L = \frac{4 R^3}{3 r^2} = \frac{4 \times 27}{3 \times 0.01} = 3600$ cm $= 36$ m — watch the mm-to-cm step.

questions.q: What is the value of $\tan 20^\circ \tan 30^\circ \tan 40^\circ \tan 50^\circ \tan 60^\circ \tan 70^\circ$?
questions.solution:
Pair complementary angles: $\tan 20^\circ \tan 70^\circ = 1$, $\tan 40^\circ \tan 50^\circ = 1$, $\tan 30^\circ \tan 60^\circ = 1$.
Product $= 1$.

**Answer: 1**
questions.shortcut: $\tan\theta \cdot \tan(90^\circ - \theta) = 1$ — pair off the six angles.

questions.q: From the foot of a tower 96 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of a building is $60^\circ$, and from the top of the tower it is $30^\circ$. What is the height of the building?
questions.solution:
Let the building's height be $H$ and the horizontal distance $d$.
$H = d \tan 60^\circ = d\sqrt{3}$ and $H - 96 = d \tan 30^\circ = \frac{d}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Subtract: $96 = d\left(\sqrt{3} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{2d}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow d = 48\sqrt{3}$, so $H = 48\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 144$ m.

**Answer: 144 m**
questions.shortcut: The tower height $= d(\tan 60^\circ - \tan 30^\circ) = \frac{2d}{\sqrt{3}}$, giving $d = 48\sqrt{3}$ and $H = 144$ m.

questions.q: The area of a circular park is 1386 m². What is its circumference? [Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution:
$\pi r^2 = 1386 \Rightarrow r^2 = 1386 \times \frac{7}{22} = 441 \Rightarrow r = 21$ m.
Circumference $= 2\pi r = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = 132$ m.

**Answer: 132 m**
questions.shortcut: $r = \sqrt{441} = 21$, then $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 21 = 132$.
questions.pattern: area to circumference of a circle

questions.q: The mean of the numbers $9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21$ and $m$ is $m$ itself. What is the value of $m$?
questions.solution:
Sum $= 8m$, and the seven known numbers add to $105$.
$105 + m = 8m \Rightarrow 7m = 105 \Rightarrow m = 15$.

**Answer: 15**
questions.shortcut: Mean equal to the unknown means: sum of the others = 7 × unknown.

questions.q: The numbers $8, 12, 16, x, 26, 30$ are in ascending order. If their median is 19, what is the value of $x$?
questions.solution:
For six numbers the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: $\frac{16 + x}{2} = 19$.
$16 + x = 38 \Rightarrow x = 22$ (and $16 < 22 < 26$, so the order holds).

**Answer: 22**
questions.shortcut: Median of an even set = average of the two middle terms.
questions.pattern: even-count median gives the missing value

questions.q: What is the median of the numbers $7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 4, 8$?
questions.solution:
Arranged in order: $3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11$ — seven numbers.
The median is the 4th value $= 7$.

**Answer: 7**
questions.shortcut: Sort, then take the middle of the odd count.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of scooters produced by a factory in five months of a year:

| Month | Scooters produced |
|---|---|
| January | 220 |
| February | 260 |
| March | 180 |
| April | 240 |
| May | 300 |

What is the average monthly production over these five months?
questions.shortcut: Deviations from 240: $-20, +20, -60, 0, +60$ cancel to zero — the average is 240.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of scooters produced by a factory in five months of a year:

| Month | Scooters produced |
|---|---|
| January | 220 |
| February | 260 |
| March | 180 |
| April | 240 |
| May | 300 |

What is the percentage increase in production from March to May?
questions.solution:
Increase $= 300 - 180 = 120$ on a base of $180$.
Percentage increase $= \frac{120}{180} \times 100 = 66\frac{2}{3}\%$.

**Answer: $66\frac{2}{3}\%$**
questions.shortcut: $\frac{2}{3}$ of 100% $= 66\frac{2}{3}\%$ straight from the fraction table.
